The word bust is interesting because it wears many different hats depending on the situation. It has several completely unrelated meanings, so the only way to fully understand it is to learn each one in its own context. Here they are.
Meaning 1: A sculpture of someone's upper body

This is the oldest and most literal meaning. A bust is a three-dimensional artwork — made of marble, bronze, clay, or similar materials — that shows a person's head, neck, shoulders, and upper chest, but stops there. Nothing below the chest is included. Museums are filled with busts of historical figures: Roman emperors, philosophers, kings. The artwork sits on a flat base or pedestal. So when you walk into a library and see a stone carving of Abraham Lincoln showing just his face and shoulders on a stand, that object is called a bust.
Meaning 2: The chest area of the body (and its measurement)

When referring to the human body — particularly a woman's body — bust means the chest, specifically the breast area. In clothing and fashion, it refers to the measurement around the fullest part of the chest. When a dress label says "Bust: 36 inches," it means the circumference of the chest at its widest point. This meaning is used both for the physical body part ("she has a large bust") and for the number you get when you measure it ("what is your bust size?").
Meaning 3: A complete failure or disappointment

In everyday informal English, a bust means something that fails, flops, or turns out to be a total waste. If you organize a big party and nobody shows up, it was "a bust." If a new product launches with huge hype but nobody buys it, it was "a bust." If an investment makes no money and collapses, it "went bust." This meaning carries a specific feeling: something that seemed promising but delivered absolutely nothing. The emphasis is always on total failure, not mild disappointment.
Meaning 4: A police arrest or raid

In informal English — especially American English — a bust means an arrest by police, or a police raid on a location. "A drug bust" means police raided a place specifically to catch people selling or using illegal drugs. "He got a bust last night" means he was arrested. You'll see this word constantly in news headlines and crime dramas. It's widely understood and used, even if it's not formal language.
Meaning 5: A period of economic collapse (the opposite of a "boom")

In economics, a bust refers to a sharp and painful period of economic decline. Businesses fail, people lose jobs, prices crash, and the overall economy shrinks. This meaning almost always appears alongside its opposite — "boom" — which refers to a period of rapid economic growth and prosperity. The phrase "boom and bust" describes how economies naturally go through cycles of rise and fall. The Great Depression of the 1930s, for example, was one of history's most devastating busts.

In the card game blackjack, a bust is when a player draws cards that push their total above 21. If your cards add up to 22 or more, you've "gone bust" — and you automatically lose that round, regardless of what the dealer has. The word perfectly captures what happens: you pushed too far and it all fell apart.
Meaning 7: A hard punch or blow

Less commonly, but still in use, bust can mean a hard hit or punch. "He took a bust to the jaw" means he was punched hard in the jaw. This usage is informal and typically refers to a sharp, sudden physical strike. You'll hear it more in older American English and in certain regional dialects.
The thread that ties most of these together

If you look at meanings 3 through 7, there's a common spirit running through them: something breaking down, collapsing, or being forcefully stopped. The police bust breaks up illegal activity. The economic bust breaks down financial growth. The blackjack bust breaks your game. The punch busts your face. Even the informal use of "that was a bust" carries the feeling of something falling apart. The sculpture meaning (1) and the chest measurement meaning (2) stand completely apart from this — they're their own separate ideas.

Once you recognize the context, identifying the right meaning becomes easy. Is someone talking about art or a museum? Meaning 1. Clothing or body shape? Meaning 2. Something that failed? Meaning 3. Police action? Meaning 4. The economy? Meaning 5. A card game? Meaning 6. A fight? Meaning 7.
